notes: Identity verified from supplied canonical text: title From Power to Inaction: Ambivalence Gives Pause to the Powerful; Geoffrey R. O. Durso, Pablo Briñol, and Richard E. Petty; Psychological Science 2016, 27(12), 1660–1666; DOI 10.1177/0956797616669947. This is a full primary research-report text with methods, results, discussion, and references, not an abstract or secondary account. No PDF path was supplied; no acquisition or rendering was performed. Target uncertainty: assigned study_o=1 and description Relationship between ambivalence and pausing among the powerful do not distinguish subjective preference for inaction from behavioral decision time, interaction from simple contrast, or explain use of pooled experiments. Printed critical tests pool Experiments 1 and 2; no Study-1-specific coefficient is established by the locator. An ambivalent-versus-univalent contrast specifically within high power is also not identified by the printed simple effects (which compare high versus low power within profile). Do not select by numeric agreement. Candidate pooled tests, all printed partial eta squared (canonical notation ηp2), not unqualified eta squared: preference interaction F(1, 305)=10.74, p=.001, ηp2=.034; preference high-versus-low power within ambivalent profile F(1, 142)=8.47, p=.004, ηp2=.056; behavioral interaction F(1, 305)=4.40, p=.037, ηp2=.014; behavioral high-versus-low power within ambivalent profile F(1, 142)=4.11, p=.044, ηp2=.028; joint multivariate interaction F(2, 304)=6.44, p=.002, ηp2=.041. Each listed p is an exact equality attached to its own candidate effect. Sample candidates: 126 Experiment-1 participants after 3 nonserious-response exclusions, versus 125 Experiment-1 participants after 1 further decision-time outlier exclusion; the combined final sample is explicitly printed as 313 (125 Experiment 1 and 188 Experiment 2). No subgroup N inferred from degrees of freedom, no sum adopted as target N, and no metric conversion performed. Unassigned replication and success fields are placeholders.
